title: When the Vow Sings
premise: Ten years ago, Gideon Yarrow's testimony helped convict his best friend, Callum, of arson at the Yarrow vineyard — a verdict that also ended his engagement to Callum's sister, Odette. When a snowstorm traps Gideon, Odette, and a newly pardoned Callum at the estate during the winter wine festival, the old fire's true cause resurfaces in the cellar ledgers, and Gideon must choose between protecting his name and speaking the sentence he has rehearsed for a decade: 'I lied, and it was for me, not against you.' His confession clears Callum, costs him the vineyard, and earns him something better — Odette, who finally stops loving him in the past tense.
about_author: Zephyrine Joubert is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent six winters working cellar doors in the Loire Valley before turning to fiction. She writes love stories set among vines, debts, and the things people confess only when snowed in.

chapters.title: Frost on the Ledger
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Days before the winter festival, Gideon audits the vineyard's crushing debts and finds an old cellar ledger with an entry that doesn't match his decade-old testimony about the arson. The emotional beat is dread: the past he buried is knocking, and the festival guests are already arriving.

chapters.title: Three at the Gate
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. The snowstorm strands Odette and her brother Callum — pardoned after ten years — at Gideon's estate. Old love and old accusations collide over mulled wine; Callum hints he knows who really set the fire. The beat is charged tension: three rivals for the truth, one roof, no way out.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Callum reveals the ledger proves the fire was set by Gideon's late uncle to claim insurance — and that Gideon's testimony was coerced to protect the family name. Confronted, Gideon flees to the frozen vineyard; Odette follows. The beat is the climax: in the snow, he finally speaks the rehearsed sentence aloud.

chapters.title: The Vow, Sung
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. At the festival's closing night, Gideon publicly withdraws his testimony, signs the vineyard over toward restitution, and lets the town judge him. Callum walks free and forgiven; Odette, watching him choose justice over inheritance, takes his hand in the present tense. The beat is release: love, finally unburdened.
